pages.title: Welcome, tinker
pages.text:
Robotica is about robots that do the boring work, so you can explore, fight and build.

You start in the stone age. Copper, wood and cobblestone are enough for your first robot. No iron needed.

Every item in this book has a recipe: click its icon to see it, then click the ingredients to follow the chain down.

pages.title: Your first day
pages.text:
1. Mine copper. A vein gives plenty.
2. Craft Copper Gears, then a Clockwork Mechanism and a Wooden Chassis.
3. Build a Winding Crank and a Mainspring. Put the spring in the crank and right-click until it is wound.
4. Build Stumpy, place it near some saplings, give it the Mainspring.

Stumpy now chops, replants and collects for about two hours of work.

pages.title: Batteries
pages.text:
Robots carry a cell. A Mainspring lasts about 2 hours of work, a Copper Cell 8, a Redstone Cell 24 and an Ender Cell 72.

A robot with nothing to do barely drains. Once you have power, cables and Chargers keep everything topped up.

pages.title: Five ages
pages.text:
Age 0 Clockwork: wood, stone, copper.
Age 1 Wired: iron, redstone, gold.
Age 2 Servo: diamonds, obsidian, quartz and a Servo Core.
Age 3 Deep: netherite, blaze rods and a Magma Core.
Age 4 Antigrav: ender pearls, nether stars and an Antigrav Core.

Cores will drop from bosses. Until the bosses arrive they have an expensive recipe.

pages.title: The parts ladder
pages.text:
Robotica machines are built from parts, and each age's parts are built from the age before. A Reinforced Casing eats four Iron Casings, which eat eight iron each.

Starting something is cheap. Making it great costs a lot. Plan your iron.

pages.title: Circuits and motors
pages.text: Circuits and motors follow the same ladder. Iron Plates come from a Tinker's Hammer (two ingots per plate) or a Metal Press (one ingot per plate). Plates from other mods work too.

pages.title: Making FE
pages.text:
Robotica uses Forge Energy (FE), the same power as Thermal, Mekanism and most tech mods. Their generators can power your robots and Robotica generators can power their machines.

Combustion Generator: burns fuel, 40 FE/t.
Solar Panel: 8 FE/t by day, Mk2 32 FE/t.

pages.title: Moving and storing FE
pages.text:
Conduits carry FE between blocks. Copper moves 256 FE/t, Gold 1,024 FE/t.

Accumulators store it and output on their front face. They keep their charge when broken.

The Charger fills cells and tools.

pages.title: Metal Press
pages.text: Turns one ingot into one plate. Twice as efficient as the hammer, and it takes speed upgrades.

pages.title: Stumpy and Sprout
pages.text:
Stumpy fells whole trees, replants and picks up drops. Sprout harvests and replants crops.

Both push their output into a chest, Supply Crate, or a Refined Storage or AE2 interface next to them.

pages.title: Farm tiers
pages.text:
Right-click a placed farm bot with a Farm Kit to upgrade it in place.

Mk1: 9x9, slow, +50% growth.
Mk2: 13x13, faster, double growth.
Mk3: 17x17, fast, triple growth.
Mk4: 25x25, the whole area every pulse, five times growth.

pages.title: Digging a real hole
pages.text:
The Excavator mines everything below it down to bedrock. It starts small and slow: 8x8, one block every two seconds.

It seals fluids as it goes, skips chests and other block entities, and never touches bedrock.

pages.title: Upgrade cards
pages.text:
Cards go in upgrade slots of machines and robots.

Range: 16, 32, 48, 64 square.
Speed: 2x, 4x, 10x, 20x.
Efficiency: less energy per block.
Fortune (Age 2+) and Silk Touch.
Void: deletes cobblestone and other junk.

Each level is crafted from the level below plus that age's parts.

pages.title: Mining tools
pages.text:
Tinker's Hammer (Age 0): 3x3, slower than a pickaxe.
Bore Drill (Age 1): 3x3 on FE.
Servo Drill (Age 2): 5x5 and vein mining.
Magma Drill (Age 3): 3x3x3, 9x9, auto-smelt.
Null Drill (Age 4): up to 12x12x12.

FE tools never break. Empty, they mine like a wooden pickaxe.

pages.title: Controls
pages.text:
V: cycle mode. Sneak + scroll does the same.
Hold sneak: always mine one block.
B: swap Silk Touch and Fortune.
G: settings for the tool in your hand (keep floor, auto-pickup, void filter, auto-smelt, light placer).

An outline shows what will break before you swing.

pages.title: Trees
pages.text: The Felling Axe (Age 0) and Chainsaw (Age 1) cut a whole tree at once. The axe pays with durability per log, the chainsaw with FE.

pages.title: Upgrading tools
pages.text: Tools upgrade at a smithing table: an Upgrade Kit as template, the old tool, and that age's core. Energy and settings carry over.

pages.title: Arsenal
pages.text:
Gearblade (Age 0): a fast copper sword.
Shock Baton (Age 1): slows what it hits.
Rivet Gun (Age 2): rapid fire, no ammo, FE per shot.
Arc Blade (Age 3): lightning jumps to three nearby monsters.
Null Lance (Age 4): hold to charge, then a beam through everything in a line.

pages.title: Architect Table
pages.text:
Feed the table cobblestone, wood, glass, ingots or gems. It turns them into matter: rustic, refined and exotic.

Pick a plot on the grid, pick a room, and the table builds it out of Robotica blocks it fabricates from matter and FE. You never craft the blocks one by one.

pages.title: Styles
pages.text:
Timberframe (Age 0) costs only rustic matter. Copper Works (Age 1), Steel Lab (Age 2) and Null Spire (Age 4) cost more and look better.

Every building block also has a normal recipe, so you can repair or extend a room by hand.

pages.title: Capturing essence
pages.text:
Right-click a hostile mob with an Essence Vial to take a sample. Eight samples of the same mob fill the vial.

Bosses cannot be sampled.

pages.title: The replicator
pages.text:
Build a 3x3x3 frame with the Replicator Controller in the middle of one side and at least one Replicator Glass. Insert a full vial and power it.

Harvest mode drops loot into the controller as if you killed the mob. Spawn mode makes the real mob for your own grinder. It is slow and hungry: about one cycle a minute.

pages.title: Warp Pads
pages.text: Name a Warp Pad, stand on it and right-click to travel to any pad you own or that a friend made public. FE cost grows with distance. A Rift Upgrade lets a pad jump between dimensions.

pages.title: Going home
pages.text:
Sneak-right-click a pad with a Recall Remote to bind it. Hold right-click for three seconds to go home. Getting hit cancels it.

Portal Gates (Age 4) are walk-through portals between two linked gates, in any dimension.
